draft.title: Mitosis
card: Mitosis is a type of cell division. One parent cell divides to make two daughter cells that are genetically identical to it and to each other.

Before mitosis, the cell copies its DNA. Each daughter cell then receives a full set of chromosomes, so the chromosome number stays the same. A human body cell with 46 chromosomes makes two cells with 46 each.
Mitosis happens in body cells, not sex cells. It adds cells for growth and replaces cells that are damaged or worn out, such as skin cells after a graze.
Single-celled organisms such as amoebae can also use a form of cell division like this to reproduce. Their offspring are identical to the parent.
draft.remember: Mitosis: one cell makes two identical cells with the same chromosome number, for growth and repair.

a.q: A skin cell with 46 chromosomes divides by mitosis to heal a graze. What are the daughter cells like?
opts: Two cells with 46 chromosomes each, identical to the parent
Two cells with 23 chromosomes each, identical to each other
Four cells with 23 chromosomes each, different from each other
Four cells with 46 chromosomes each, different from the parent
a.why: Mitosis makes two daughter cells that are identical to the parent, with the full chromosome number of 46. The second option is tempting because the cells would be identical to each other, but the chromosome number is not halved in mitosis.
a.clue: Think about the number of cells made and whether the chromosome number changes.

b.q: Liam cuts his hand, and over the next week the wound closes. Which statement best explains how mitosis helps?
opts: It makes new cells identical to old ones to replace damage
It makes new cells with half the chromosomes for variation
It makes sex cells that carry repair instructions to the cut
It changes the DNA of nearby cells so they match each other
b.why: Mitosis makes genetically identical body cells, which replace the damaged ones. Halving the chromosome number and adding variation do not happen in mitosis, and the second option describes a different type of division.
b.clue: Repair needs new cells that match the existing tissue.
